A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPTQ–Babai equivalence study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison. v2 retains the original derivations while substantially extending the theory and applications.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical proofs, algorithm pseudocode and illustrative lattice diagrams, but no original empirical outcomes. Appendix B derives an expectation under a uniform prior; it does not report a simulation or data analysis.

after.justification: v2 reports original Qwen3 quantization evaluations, Hessian-trace measurements comparing quantization orders, and SSQR GPU timing experiments in Section 5 and Appendices C.3 and D.

M1.justification: v2 retains batched Babai quantization and min-pivot ordering, and adds two substantive methods. SSQR adjusts scales to meet an outlier-density target while preserving overflow residuals in floating point. HPTQ quantizes to unclipped integers and searches for a scale meeting a Huffman-coded bit budget (Section 5; Algorithms 9–11).

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical dataset or task coverage. v2 adds FineWeb-Edu calibration, WikiText-2 and C4 perplexity evaluation, and zero-shot evaluation on WinoGrande, MMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, SciQ and TruthfulQA. It also evaluates GPU inference performance (Appendix D).

E2.justification: v1 discusses algorithms without empirical comparisons. v2 evaluates GPTQ, RTN, HRTN and BF16 alongside the proposed quantizers in Tables 3 and 5, compares SSQR runtime against PyTorch BF16, and compares min-pivot with front-to-back, back-to-front, random and act-order permutations in Table 2. SpQR itself has no reported comparator row.

E3.justification: v2 introduces experimental protocols absent from v1: 256 calibration sequences of 2048 tokens, specified perplexity preprocessing, Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 14B, bitwidth and outlier-budget sweeps, act-order, and group size 128 for RTN/GPTQ/SSQR. Timing includes batch-one decoding of 128 new tokens and layer benchmarks at batch sizes 1–16. These are new experiments, not revisions to earlier experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an empirical comparison of five quantization orders using tr(D), testing the bound-related proxy behind v1's untested min-pivot proposal. Figures 4–5 additionally examine SSQR sensitivity to outlier density, inlier bitwidth, batch size and layer shape. v1 contains no corresponding empirical analyses.

E5.justification: v2 reports averaging random-order trace measurements over 100 runs (Appendix C.3) and fixed-seed calibration shuffling (Appendix D.2), whereas v1 has no empirical run or seed reporting. These are newly reported practices, not an established increase in runs. Confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: v2 adds the empirical results in Tables 2–11 and Figures 4–5. For example, Table 3 reports Qwen3-8B WikiText-2/C4 perplexities of 10.34/14.23 for HPTQ versus 12.77/15.61 for GPTQ at 3.125 average bits. Figure 4(c) reports roughly 2× SSQR decoding speedup over PyTorch BF16 at batch one. These are newly reported comparisons; v1 supplies no matching empirical scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal OBQ projection theorem and dimension-selection corollary with proofs (Section 4.2), a geometric proof of GPTQ–Babai equivalence, and a relative approximation bound with its derivation (Theorem 5; Appendix C.1). The original algebraic equivalence proof, absolute bound and one-third expected-error derivation are retained and reorganized, rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: v1's central contributions are the geometric equivalence, error guarantee and ordering heuristic. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion additionally claim practical no-clipping quantizers with better accuracy than original GPTQ and efficient GPU inference kernels. This substantially expands the claimed contribution beyond theoretical analysis and prospective applications.

C2.justification: v2 explains why enlarging scales to eliminate clipping can worsen the error bound and motivates explicit outlier handling. It qualifies min-pivot's practical benefit as modest and recommends act-order as an inexpensive approximation for well-conditioned Hessians (Sections 4.5–5). Appendix D.4 adds kernel tradeoff interpretations, although its claim of superiority in every setting conflicts with sub-baseline results in Figure 5.

D1.justification: v2 adds scale-search pseudocode and boundaries, calibration and evaluation processing details, a typical damping formula, and extensive SSQR CUDA/C++ implementation information. Appendix D.4 describes weight reordering, sparse-outlier storage, SIMT versus tensor-core execution, numerical precision and hardware. v1 provides general quantization pseudocode without these experimental or kernel details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Birnick's concurrent equivalence paper with a priority footnote, positions SSQR relative to SpQR, cites ICQuant for outlier motivation, and adds several background references. v1's explicit comparison of its bound with QuIP is removed, while the underlying Hessian-based compression and lattice-algorithm positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and contribution narrative, expands OBQ and Babai explanations, and adds a geometric-to-algebraic proof roadmap. It reorganizes the paper into theoretical results and applications, moves batched Babai construction and bound derivations into appendices, and adds a table of contents. These changes substantially alter the explanatory structure.

P2.justification: v2 reorders Figure 1's basis-reduction and projection panels and revises its caption. It adds geometric illustrations in Figures 2–3, multipanel experimental plots in Figures 4–5, and Tables 1–11 covering the quantization–CVP dictionary, ordering measurements and benchmark results. Retained pseudocode and proof displays are also relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the connection between the lattice analysis and practical quantization. It adds explicit geometric and relative-bound derivations, empirically examines v1's untested ordering heuristic, and supports new overflow-tolerant methods with accuracy and timing evidence (Appendices C–D). The blanket kernel-superiority statement is overstated: Figure 5 includes batch-16 slowdowns. That reporting flaw limits the performance claim but does not outweigh the substantial gains in explanation and demonstrated practical relevance.
